scope: Review of the next 15 alphabetically pending active catalog entries, Browse AI through Chroma. Fourteen were accepted after first-party checks. Character.AI was moved to status watch because its official court-supervised sale process leaves service continuity unresolved; the company explicitly says the platform remains operational for now.

accepted.name: Browse AI
accepted.description: AI-assisted no-code web data extraction and monitoring: Table Studio proposes structured tables from a URL, while Robot Studio records interactive browser steps and scheduled robots track changes.
accepted.userValue: For teams that need recurring structured website data—such as product details, listings, leads or competitor changes—without maintaining custom scrapers.

accepted.name: Browser Use
accepted.description: Open-source Python/TypeScript browser-agent framework with hosted agents and managed cloud browsers; agents navigate pages, fill forms, extract data and replay successful workflows.
accepted.userValue: For developers and teams automating multi-step browser tasks with a local or hosted agent and optional managed browser infrastructure.

accepted.name: Browserbase
accepted.description: Managed web-agent platform providing scalable browser sessions, Search and Fetch, Agent Identity, observability and integrations such as the Stagehand browser automation SDK.
accepted.userValue: For developers deploying agents that must interact with live websites reliably, with managed sessions, authentication support, logs, live view and replay.

accepted.name: Bubble AI
accepted.description: Bubble's AI app builder turns natural-language requirements into an app structure with pages, workflows and a database, then lets users refine the result in Bubble's visual editor.
accepted.userValue: For founders and nontechnical builders who want a functional web-app starting point while retaining visual control over the interface, data and logic.

accepted.name: Buffer AI Assistant
accepted.description: An AI writing feature inside Buffer's Create workspace and publishing composer that drafts social posts, generates ideas, adjusts tone and repurposes longer content using language models.
accepted.userValue: For creators and social teams that want to draft and adapt posts inside the same publishing and scheduling workflow. This is a Buffer feature, not a claim that Buffer's core platform is AI-powered.

accepted.name: Builder.io Visual Copilot
accepted.description: Builder's AI design-to-code capability converts Figma designs into responsive frontend code and can map generated output to a team's existing components, design tokens and frameworks.
accepted.userValue: For product teams that want to turn approved designs into code aligned with their real component system, then refine and review the implementation in their existing repository workflow.

accepted.name: Caktus AI
accepted.description: Academic study workspace with AI tools for essay drafting with source citations, research, document analysis, step-by-step math and science help, notes and study materials.
accepted.userValue: For students who need one academic workflow for researching, drafting and understanding course material; generated citations should still be checked against the original sources.

accepted.name: CAMEL-AI
accepted.description: Open-source multi-agent framework and research ecosystem for building agent societies, task automation, data generation, tool use, memory and retrieval-augmented workflows.
accepted.userValue: For developers and researchers prototyping coordinated agents, agent collaboration and multi-agent simulations with a documented framework and examples.

accepted.name: CapCut AI
accepted.description: AI features within CapCut's video editor, including text- and image-to-video generation, AI voice and other editing assistance that can be refined in the same editing workflow.
accepted.userValue: For creators who want to generate or enhance video assets and finish short-form content in an integrated editor. This is an AI feature suite within CapCut.

accepted.name: Captions
accepted.description: AI video editor for generating and editing creator videos, with automated cuts, B-roll, captions, translation, AI avatars and digital twins, plus prompt-based editing.
accepted.userValue: For creators producing short-form videos, ads and tutorials who want AI-assisted post-production and localized versions in one app.

accepted.name: Cartesia
accepted.description: Speech AI platform offering Sonic text-to-speech, Ink speech-to-text and managed voice agents, with streaming APIs and cloud, on-premise and on-device deployment options.
accepted.userValue: For developers building real-time voice interfaces and phone agents that need low-latency speech generation and transcription.

accepted.name: Cerebras Inference
accepted.description: Hosted inference API for supported open-weight language models running on Cerebras systems, with OpenAI-compatible access and developer and enterprise deployment tiers.
accepted.userValue: For developers who need fast managed language-model inference without operating their own model-serving infrastructure.

accepted.name: Chatbase
accepted.description: Platform for building and deploying AI agents trained on a company's website and documents, with actions, analytics, testing and deployment across chat, email, voice and messaging channels.
accepted.userValue: For businesses that need customer-support or product-guidance agents grounded in their own content and connected to helpdesk, commerce or communication workflows.

accepted.name: Chroma
accepted.description: Open-source AI data infrastructure for storing documents and embeddings, performing dense, sparse and hybrid vector search and metadata filtering, with self-hosted and managed cloud options.
accepted.userValue: For developers building RAG, semantic search or multimodal retrieval systems who need a local or hosted vector database.

statusWatch.name: Character.AI
statusWatch.reason: Character.ai's official October 12, 2026 announcement says the platform remains up and running during a voluntary Chapter 11 process and court-supervised sale, but also says the platform will be wound down if no actionable bid emerges. As of 2026-10-31, the sale outcome is unresolved. This is a continuity risk, not evidence that the service has already shut down.
statusWatch.nextAction: Recheck the official sale-process updates and confirm a buyer and continued service, or a formal wind-down notice, after the process expected to conclude by the end of November or early December 2026.

notes: Browser Use and Browserbase are adjacent but distinct: Browser Use supplies an open-source browser-agent library and hosted agents, while Browserbase supplies managed browser infrastructure and agent web-access services.

Bubble AI, Buffer AI Assistant, Builder.io Visual Copilot and CapCut AI are first-party AI capabilities within broader platforms, not separate claims that the parent platforms are entirely AI-powered. Each is retained because the capability solves a specific, documented user workflow.
Buffer's own product page says Buffer's core scheduling and publishing features are not AI-powered; only the optional AI Assistant feature is represented in this catalog entry.
Caktus AI's academic writing and study claims are described by task type only; no company-reported user counts or unverifiable superiority claims were copied into the catalog.

Character.ai's October 12, 2026 notice says service remains up and running during Chapter 11 and a court-supervised sale, while warning that the platform will be wound down if no actionable bid emerges. It is unresolved, not marked discontinued.
